Article Title: At 18, Salman Khan lost his father, drove taxi for months before becoming an Army man and now an Asian Games rowing medallist
Article Text:
Indian rowers Satnam Singh and Salman Khan pose with their bronze medal (PTI Photo)

Salman lost his father at 18

A friend's advice changed his life

How Salman became a rower

The turning point

From national gold to international success

From driving a cab to wearing the India jersey

For rower Salman Khan , winning an Asian Games medal is the latest chapter in a journey that began with family responsibilities, financial struggles and a job as a cab driver.The Indian rower won the bronze medal in the men's double sculls event alongside teammate Satnam Singh at the Asian Games 2026 on Thursday. The Indian pair stayed in second place until the 1,500m mark before slipping to third in the final 500m. They finished the race in 6:13.25 at the Nagaragawa International Regatta Course.China's Yi Xudi and Yide Nie won gold with a timing of 6:09.37, while Uzbekistan's Pavel Sorin and Mekhrojbek Mamatkulov took silver in 6:10.49.For Salman, the medal has come after years of hard work and a life that could have taken a very different path.Salman was born in Pure Dhingai in Amethi district of Uttar Pradesh. His father, Mohammed Kasim Khan, worked in truck-body construction in Tauru, Haryana, where Salman completed his schooling.He was the eldest of four brothers and two sisters. When his father died of dengue, Salman was just 18 years old.With his younger siblings still studying, the responsibility of supporting the family fell on him. His dream of joining the Army had to take a backseat as earning a livelihood became his priority.Salman started driving an Uber cab in Delhi. He worked day and night to keep his family going.Salman had not given up completely on his Army dream. One day, while resting after a shift, a close friend reminded him that his height and physical build could help him in the Army. That advice pushed him to try again.He handed over the cab to another driver and spent four months preparing through hard running and training. He cleared the recruitment rally, medical and written examinations.In September 2018, he joined the Bombay Engineer Group (BEG), Kirkee, Pune.At the training centre, coaches noticed Salman's height and physique and introduced him to rowing. He knew nothing about the sport and initially had no interest in taking it up. With his family's financial situation, sport was not something he thought he could pursue.He refused several times. But the coaches continued to push him and eventually put him in a boat. They saw potential in him and began training him seriously.Salman's first inter-centre regatta gave him the first sign that he could make something out of rowing. He won a silver medal, which gave him confidence.The next major step came in 2021 when Salman cleared the ergometer benchmarks and was selected for the Army Rowing Node at CME Pune. Training alongside some of India's best rowers changed his outlook.What had started as a sport he did not even want to take up became something he wanted to pursue professionally.Salman began to believe that rowing could help him win medals for India.Salman's progress continued over the next few years. At the 36th National Games in Gujarat in 2022, he won gold. At the 2023 Senior Nationals, he won gold in the single sculls against Olympian Dattu Bhokanal. That performance helped him earn a place in the India camp.In 2024, Salman won his first international gold at the Asian Rowing Cup in South Korea with Nitin Deol. That victory also earned him a promotion to Naib Subedar in the Indian Army.He followed it with a silver at the 2025 Australian Rowing Championships and another silver at the 2025 Asian Rowing Championships.Those performances helped him secure his place in India's Asian Games squad.For Salman, representing India carries a special meaning because of where his journey started. He came from a village background and had to take responsibility for his family at a very young age.His mother, Jabrun Nisha, remained a major source of strength for him, while his wife, Sahiba Khatoon, supported him throughout his journey.His coaches and support staff also played a major role in keeping him on the rowing path, particularly during periods when he lost interest in the sport.At the Army Rowing Node, officers and coaches helped him regain his focus and develop as an athlete.Salman's journey from Amethi to the Indian Army, and from an unfamiliar boat to an Asian Games medal, has been built over years of perseverance, discipline and the support of his family, coaches and teammates.
Article Summary: Salman Khan won a bronze medal in the men's double sculls at the Asian Games 2026 on Thursday. The Indian pair stayed in second place until the 1,500m mark before slipping to third in the final 500m. China's Yi Xudi and Yide Nie won gold with a timing of 6:09.37, while Uzbekistan's Pavel Sorin and Mekhrojbek Mamatkulov took silver.

Article Title: LoP's presence in panel to pick CEC, ECs 'ornamental': SC judge
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Deliberating on the validity of the law on appointment of chief election commissioner and election commissioners by a panel of the PM, a cabinet minister and the leader of opposition, Justice Dipankar Datta on Wednesday pointed out drawbacks and said it gave "overwhelming" power to the executive and made the presence of the LoP "ornamental", undermining the appearance of independence in the selection process. He also noted that since independence, govts had tried to control the poll body."Over seven decades, every dispensation wresting office found it convenient to keep institutions which the Constitution envisioned to be independent under their control. To enact a law on the lines empowered by Article 324(2) would have meant freeing the ECI from exclusive executive control and inviting trouble for the ruling regime. To the mind of this court, this has not been the failing of any one party or one period. A consistent trait of political power, discernible over the decades, has been to preserve leverage over the very body that is meant to judge its claim to power," Justice Datta said.He said if free and fair elections were to be ensured, it was axiomatic that the EC must not only be an independent body but also be seen to act independently and it was "painful to note that not a single party in power, entrusted by the people of India to govern this great nation", took the initiative of enacting a law of the nature which Article 324(2) left to the supreme law-making body, ie Parliament, to legislate.Also read: SC refers law on EC appointment to larger bench; decision comes amid row over EC functioning "Placing its own electoral fortunes in the hands of a truly independent arbiter was not favoured by any political party, for obvious reasons. To remain in power, the consistent pursuit through executive action has indeed been simple - influence the composition of the EC, control the process of appointment of CEC and ECs and, thereby, temper adverse electoral outcomes," Justice Datta said.Summarising the contentions raised against the law, he added, "The bottom line of the argument runs thus: it would not be a fallacious metaphor if it is said that since the umpire is picked by the captain of one side in a cricket match and his team wins, even if the decisions taken by such umpire are correct, it has the patina of suspicion, for, at the end of the day, the umpire has effectively been chosen by the winning captain. "Justice Datta further said, "There can be no gainsaying that free and fair elections, to a large extent, depend on a truly independent EC. It is not enough for the EC to be independent, it must also appear to be independent. The minister nominated by the prime minister, to function as the third member on the selection committee chaired by the prime minister, cannot be expected to defy his own nominator. In such a circumstance, the inclusion of a minister in the selection committee fails to provide the independent counterweight that a neutral selector could and he would merely echo the voice of his leader; and, consequently, the presence of the leader of opposition in the selection committee becomes largely ornamental, without furthering the purpose of his inclusion. "
Article Summary: Justice Dipankar Datta said the law gave "overwhelming" power to the executive. He also noted that since independence, govts had tried to control the poll body. He said it was axiomatic that the EC must not only be an independent body but also be seen to act independently.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu industries minister S Keerthana was subjected to sexist remarks by DMK which was questioning her absence from chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s recent London visit. The remarks by DMK leader Vaishnavi has triggered a political controversy.Vijay travelled to London to flag off actor Ajith Kumar’s car race and seek fresh investments for Tamil Nadu. Keerthana, whose portfolio places her at the centre of the state’s investment-promotion efforts, was not part of the delegation.Reacting to Keerthana’s absence, Vaishnavi referred to TN minister Aadhav Arjuna’s statement that the industries minister had not travelled for “4 days due to health reasons” and questioned the reference to the four days.“Industrial minister has not come for 4 days due to health reasons, says Aadhav Arjuna! What is the explanation regarding those "4 days"? If it refers to a natural physiological change that occurs for women, like menstruation, then why should it be stated as the reason?” Vaishnavi said.She added, “Today's women athletes consider menstruation as a normal physiological process and plan their training and competitions accordingly. Doesn't even this basic understanding of women's physiology exist for a minister who oversees the sports sector?”Vaishnavi also questioned whether the actual reason for Keerthana’s absence had been clearly communicated, saying, “Especially, clearly informing the public about the real reason for a minister not attending an event is the transparent approach.”She further asked, “What is the real reason for industrial minister not coming? Will Aadhav Arjuna clarify?”Amid the controversy, TVK leader Kanimozhi Santhosh came out in support of Keerthana and said the minister had been recovering from a collarbone surgery when she missed the London visit.“As a woman, I want to say this because I witnessed it myself. I met myminister Keerthana at Kamatchi Hospital after her collarbone surgery. Doctors had advised around 20 days of rest, but within 4 days she was back at work because of her commitment to the state,” Santhosh said.She said Keerthana continued to coordinate Vijay’s London visit even while recovering in hospital.“Even while she was at hospital bed, she was coordinating the chief minister's London visit. Her first question every single day wasn't about her pain or her tablets; it was whether every company and every arrangement was on time. I told her to relax, she wouldn't,” Santhosh said.Taking aim at those who questioned the reason for Keerthana’s absence, Santhosh said, “And what struck me most is this: when minister Aadhav Sir said she was unwell for a few days, the opposition ecosystem didn't pause to ask about what was the reason, or recovery, or what she may have actually gone through. Their minds went straight to one reason: menstruation.”“That reflex, that a woman's absence can only ever mean one thing, says nothing about her and everything about your regressive mindset. Women are not defined by their cycles. We are leaders, professionals, mothers, daughters carrying illness, injury and duty all at once, and still showing up. Reducing a woman's every unexplained day to her biology is an old habit of attacking a woman's body when her work can't be faulted,” she added.Santhosh said Keerthana returned to work despite still recovering from the surgery.“4 days after, still recovering, on painkillers and still wearing a bandage, she went straight back to meeting companies and signing MoUs, one after another, without a pause,” she said.“This regressive mindset needs to stop. We should be celebrating women who continue to lead through difficult circumstances, not discussing their cycles. Women deserve better than this. Tamil Nadu deserves better than this,” Santhosh said.She concluded by apologising to Keerthana for making her medical condition public, saying, “Sorry Keerthana, I know you wanted to keep this private but I had to post this.”
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu industries minister S Keerthana was subjected to sexist remarks by DMK. DMK was questioning her absence from chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s recent London visit. Vaishnavi referred to TN minister Aadhav Arjuna's statement that the industries minister had not travelled for “4 days due to health reasons”

Article Title: EC faultlines have a long history, dating back to 1989
Article Text:
Election Commission of India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: It is not the first time that the fault lines within the Election Commission are out in the open. The trend started from the time it became a multi-member body in 1989.Two election commissioners S S Dhanoa and V S Seigell were appointed in October 1989 and joined the poll body then led by chief election commissioner (CEC) R V S Peri Sastri. Though Sastri never publicly spoke about it, it is widely believed that the new arrangement was perceived by him as a dilution in power. By January 1990, the appointment of the two commissioners was rescinded and the EC reverted to being a single—member body.In 1993, with T N Seshan as an all-powerful CEC, the commission was once again made a multi-member body with the appointment of election commissioners M S Gill and G V G Krishnamurthy. What followed was a running feud between Seshan on the one hand and Gill and Krishnamurthy on the other. Seshan viewed the appointments as a direct assault on the independence of his office and completely refused to recognize the two new commissioners. He refused to share official documents with Gill and Krishnamurthy, barred them from attending critical meetings, and would not allocate them any office work. He openly ridiculed the election commissioners in interviews, even referring to them as “two donkeys in my office”.Interestingly, it was on Seshan’s plea challenging the govt’s decision to make EC a multi-member body that the Supreme Court had, in 1995, ruled that the election commissioners and CEC were equal in status, power and decision-making authority and that the CEC was only “first among equals”.The other internal feud in EC to recall would be one between then CEC N Gopalaswami and election commissioner Navin Chawla between 2006 and 2009. Months before he was to step down upon the end of his tenure, Gopalaswami wrote to the President of India recommending the removal of Chawla on grounds of a pro-Congress bias. In his note to the President, Gopalaswami alleged that Chawla was passing on details of EC’s meetings to senior Congress leaders, often taking “toilet breaks” during commission meetings to do so. Gopalaswami’s recommendation was however turned down by the Manmohan Singh govt and Chawla succeeded him as CEC.During the 2019 general election, the differences between then CEC Sunil Arora and then election commissioner Ashok Lavasa came to the fore, with media reports alleging that he had dissented in cases relating to complaints of alleged model code of conduct violations by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and then BJP president Amit Shah, but was overruled without the commission making his dissent noted public. EC put out a clarification that dissent notes were only made public in quasi-judicial orders passed by EC.Lavasa resigned on August 18, 2020, two years short of his tenure, and joined the Manila-headquartered Asian Development Bank (ADB) as its Vice-President.Arun Goyal was the last election commissioner to quit in the middle of his term. Though he had cited personal reasons in his resignation dated March 9, 2024, it was widely speculated that he was not on the best of terms with the then chief election commissioner Rajiv Kumar.
Article Summary: The fault lines within the Election Commission are out in the open. The trend started from the time it became a multi-member body in 1989. The other internal feud in EC to recall would be one between then CEC N Gopalaswami and election commissioner Navin Chawla.

| TNNJammu: A joint police team from Jammu has arrested three suspected members of Khauf gang, a Jammu-based criminal syndicate, in Delhi. The trio includes Karanjit Singh alias Gugga, a murder accused wanted in 13 FIRs, who escaped a juvenile observation home in RS Pura along with two Pakistani inmates in Feb.Addressing reporters Wednesday, SSP Jammu Joginder Singh said Gugga, a native of RS Pura’s Dablehar area, is an accused in the Gataroo gang rivalry murder case and several other FIRs involving attempted murder, assault, rioting, criminal intimidation and possession of illegal weapons. SP HQ Anna Lata Sinha and SP SOG Mohan Lal Sharma were also present at the press interaction.The other two arrested are Naresh Kumar alias Major from Arnia, and Rahul Kumar alias Sundi from Makhanpur, Bishnah. Naresh is involved in cases of violent assault, rioting and illegal possession of weapons. Rahul faces charges under the NDPS Act and Prisons Act for allegedly smuggling drugs into jail, police said. Both are closely associated with the Khauf gang.The SSP said the arrests, carried out by Jammu Police and SOG Jammu, are part of police’s ongoing efforts to trace fugitive offenders linked with organised criminal networks.He said further investigation is underway and more arrests are likely.Gugga fled the RS Pura observation home along with Ahsan Anwar of Nankana Sahib and Mohammad Sanaullah of Basti Jawewala in Pakistan’s Punjab province on Feb 16, 2026, after assaulting and firing at cops guarding the facility. Haryana Police caught the Pakistani duo at Ambala Cantonment railway station the next day and handed them over to their J&K counterparts, even as Gugga remained on the run. Pertinently, all three were undertrials in different cases and had attained majority at the time of their escape.

Article Title: CRPF to celebrate women personnel's milestones over 40 years
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Only two women have been decorated till date with Ashoka Chakra, India’s highest peacetime gallantry award, and one of them received it posthumously for the CRPF . Not only this, Kamlesh Kumari, the CRPF constable who was the first to sound an alert when a Jaish-e-Mohammad suicide squad stormed into Parliament premises in a white Ambassador on December 13, 2001, prompting the security personnel to engage and neutralise the terrorists before they could enter Parliament House, also happens to be the only CRPF personnel in the hallowed list of Ashoka Chakra awardees.On September 25, the CRPF will celebrate 40 years of selfless duty and gallant actions by women brave hearts like Kamlesh Kumari. During the commemoration event, CRPF DG GP Singh will, alongside the President of CRPF Family Welfare Association (CWA), felicitate veteran and serving women personnel for “their extraordinary contributions and sacrifice”.It was in 1986 that CRPF raised its first-ever woman combatant battalion; in 2022, two personnel from the same battalion were elevated to Inspector-General (IG) level posts, with Annie Abraham appointed as IG, Rapid Action Force, and Seema Dhundia as IG in charge of Bihar sector.As of today, women personnel hold charge of multiple CRPF sectors, including critical ones like Jammu. IPS officer Sanjukta Parashar recently became the first woman to lead the CRPF’s jungle warfare commando unit, CoBRA. As part of a conscious push by CRPF to place its woman officers in the lead and combatant roles, women personnel are currently heading sectors like Jammu, CoBRA, RAF, North East, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh as IG.In the past 40 years, women’s footprint in CRPF has expanded significantly, with six exclusive mahila battalions fully deployed across critical security grids and 64 women teams, comprising 24 personnel each, embedded in RAF for specialised crowd control and anti-riot duties. Integrated women components are also serving in frontline roles, including the dedicated Bastariya battalion raised to tackle Left-wing extremism.CRPF women personnel’s 40 years of selfless service and bravery have received due recognition. Constable Kamlesh Kumari was awarded the Ashok Chakra in 2002, constable Vimla Devi was honoured with Sena Medal and Lance Naik Rajwanti Devi received the Army Chief’s commendation for playing a critical operations role at the Elephant Pass check post in Sri Lanka in 1988. Constable Bindu Kumre has also received a gallantry medal for displaying exemplary bravery during the Srinagar airport terrorist attack in 2001.CRPF on Tuesday described the induction of women personnel in the force 40 years ago as “a pioneering step (that) broke deep-rooted barriers, redefining women’s empowerment, operational inclusivity and equal opportunity within the nation’s security framework”.
Article Summary: Only two women have been decorated till date with Ashoka Chakra, India’s highest peacetime gallantry award. On September 25, the CRPF will celebrate 40 years of selfless duty and gallant actions by women brave hearts. In 1986, CRPF raised its first-ever woman combatant battalion.

Article Title: 'UP ke ladke' in for political 'brawl'? SP, Congress spar over who can beat BJP in 2027
Article Text:
'UP ke ladke' vs each other? SP-Congress spar over who can beat BJP in 2027

Iqra Hasan ’s remarks trigger Congress pushback

BJP joins SP-Congress war of words

SP-Cong face a new test: Who gets how many seats?

Owaisi offer adds another variable

AIMIM's performance in Maharashtra, UP and Bihar

What happened in 2022 assembly polls

Big heart or bigger share?

What next for UP ke ladke?

NEW DELHI: The "UP ke ladke" bonhomie is beginning to look less like a united front and more like a contest for the upper hand, with Congress and Samajwadi Party leaders trading jabs over who can take on the BJP in Uttar Pradesh. With the 2027 assembly election approaching, are cracks emerging in the INDIA bloc's battle plan against Yogi Adityanath's BJP?SP MP Iqra Hasan set off the latest bout of sparring by saying Congress "can't achieve much on its own" and projecting party boss and former CM Akhilesh Yadav as the only leader capable of defeating the BJP in Uttar Pradesh.Her remarks drew a quick response from the Congress, with party leaders pushing back against the suggestion that the SP could take on the BJP by itself.Congress MP Imran Masood said, "She (Iqra Hasan) also cannot do it alone. What is the problem with that? Iqra is our child. She is like our niece.""People from the Trinamool Congress were also saying a lot. Look at what happened in Bengal. Let us move together, and we will remain in peace," he added with a reference to Mamata-led TMC's big defeat in Bengal after contesting solo.Congress leader Udit Raj pointed to the SP's performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha election while questioning Iqra's claim."That may be her (Iqra Hasan's) own statement, but we can understand this through an example: when the alliance was formed in 2024, the Samajwadi Party won 36 seats. What was its performance before that? The Samajwadi Party had only six MPs in 2019. So, in politics, one plus one does not always make two; one plus one can make eleven.Therefore, I think she should correct her understanding," Udit Raj told IANS.The saffron party, meanwhile, was quick to weigh in on the disagreement. Uttar Pradesh BJP vice-president Neeraj Singh said, "Congress will not be able to achieve anything on its own across the country. And even if it forms an alliance with the Samajwadi Party or any other party in Uttar Pradesh, the people of Uttar Pradesh have already formed an alliance in their hearts with the BJP government..."Iqra, who made the remarks on Monday, had said, "It is an absolutely foolish statement. I think that if there is anyone in Uttar Pradesh who can defeat the BJP, it is only Akhilesh Yadav. Congress will not be able to do anything on its own. If the alliance remains, it will be very good; if it does not, it is a loss for them (Congress), not for us."The "UP ke ladke" chemistry that helped Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav pull off a striking upset in the 2024 Lok Sabha election has yet to turn into a clear seat-sharing formula for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly polls.The two leaders have continued to share the stage on occasions, including protest for students, maintaining a public show of camaraderie. But behind that familiar chemistry, the alliance arithmetic is still taking shape.There has been no concrete discussion on how the 403 assembly seats could be divided between Congress and the Samajwadi Party.Their partnership took shape months before the 2024 Lok Sabha election, and the results that followed gave the alliance a strong political imprint.The SP contested 62 of the state's 80 Lok Sabha seats and won 37, including Faizabad, the constituency covering Ayodhya. Congress fought 17 seats and won six. Together, the two parties crossed the halfway mark of UP's Lok Sabha tally, handing the BJP a major setback in a state that sends the most MPs to Parliament.For the SP, it was very much the bigger share of the alliance pie. Akhilesh's party emerged as the largest opposition force in the state, and second largest in country, while Congress revived its presence with six seats.The result also had a powerful political backdrop. Uttar Pradesh is the home turf of chief minister Yogi Adityanath and the parliamentary constituency of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The BJP had also invested enormous political capital in Ayodhya, where the Ram temple consecration took place in January 2024 in the presence of PM Modi and RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat.Yet, months later, the BJP lost the Faizabad seat to the SP.The result turned Rahul and Akhilesh into the "UP ke ladke" of the 2024 campaign, a political pairing that seemed to have found the right formula for the state's electorate. But as the next election approaches, the partnership is facing a different kind of test: Seat-sharing.Akhilesh has repeatedly said that the SP will contest the 2027 election with the INDIA bloc partners with whom it fought the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, effectively keeping the door open for Congress. But Congress has not made a similar formal commitment. Neither Rahul Gandhi nor party president Mallikarjun Kharge has publicly announced a seat-sharing arrangement with the SP.Meanwhile, the SP is already getting its electoral machinery moving.Sources told TOI that the party's top leadership has finalised candidates for more than 100 of the 403 assembly seats, while the process is under way for the remaining constituencies. The party has not yet released a formal candidate list.SP strategists say the early exercise is deliberate, giving prospective candidates time to prepare their constituencies, build networks and hit the ground running once the campaign begins.The strategy is not entirely new. Political observers point out that the SP followed a similar approach before the 2022 assembly and 2024 Lok Sabha elections, beginning the candidate-selection process well ahead of polling but releasing the actual lists only a few months before the election.Congress, meanwhile, has indicated that it is preparing to contest all 403 seats. That ambition could make the eventual negotiatins with the SP considerably more interesting.And there is another piece on the chessboard. AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi has made an open offer to Akhilesh, potentially bringing another party into the opposition's seat-sharing calculations.If the SP chooses to engage with Owaisi, the equation could become even more complicated for an alliance that has so far largely revolved around SP and Congress.The Lok Sabha 2024 friendship was a renewed one. Just two years earlier, the grand old party and Akhilesh Yadav’s Samajwadi Party had contested the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections separately, as they sought to take on Yogi Adityanath, who was then seeking a second term as chief minister.Yogi comfortably retained his Lucknow throne, while the Samajwadi Party increased its numbers. The Congress, however, suffered a major setback, winning just 2 of the 403 assembly seats.Rahul, personally, also appeared hesitant when it came to announcing the Mahagathbandhan’s chief ministerial face in Bihar last year.He also appeared to have reservations about Tejashwi Yadav’s eagerness to project himself as the alliance’s face, as well as over seat-sharing, with a large chunk of seats going to Lalu Yadav’s Rashtriya Janata Dal.A similar story could now unfold in Uttar Pradesh, where the Congress may look to expand its footprint with an eye on the next Lok Sabha elections. Uttar Pradesh remains at the heart of national politics, making a strong presence in the state crucial for any party with larger ambitions.Akhilesh Yadav, meanwhile, would be looking to return to power in Lucknow and reclaim the chief minister’s chair.Congress’ delayed decisions and its cautious approach towards trusting allies have also been visible more recently in Tamil Nadu. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav have previously urged the Congress to show a “big heart” and back “regional players” in their home turfs.So, while the Rahul-Akhilesh bond now may still look intact in public, the real test could come away from the cameras: How many seats each party wants, how many it is willing to give up, and whether the "UP ke ladke" formula can survive the hard arithmetic of 2027.The BJP under Yogi Adityanath, meanwhile, is preparing to defend its position in Uttar Pradesh and seek another term in the state's 403-member assembly, ensuring that the opposition's alliance arithmetic will remain under close watch.With a third consecutive term in Uttar Pradesh, Yogi would match former CM Mulayam Singh Yadav's record of three consecutive terms in the state, while he already holds the record for the longest uninterrupted tenure as UP chief minister, having been in office for nearly a decade.
Article Summary: Congress and Samajwadi Party leaders trade jabs over who can take on BJP in 2027. Iqra Hasan said Congress "can't achieve much on its own" and projected Akhilesh Yadav as the only leader capable of defeating the BJP in Uttar Pradesh. Congress leader Udit Raj pointed to the SP's performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. Uttar Pradesh BJP vice-president Neeraj Singh said, "Congress will not be able to achieve anything"

Article Title: Two SC Justices urge CJI to set up five-judge bench for deciding constitutional issues; why it matters
Article Text:
A two-judge SC bench has requested the CJI to explore setting up a permanent 5-judge Constitutional Bench.

Why this matters

A two-judge Supreme Court bench, comprising Justice SC Sharma and Justice Datta, has requested the Chief Justice of India to explore the possibility of setting up a permanent five-judge Constitutional Bench to deal with questions involving interpretation of the Constitution.Constitutional questions currently require bench formation: Under Article 145(3), cases involving a "substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution" must be heard by at least five judges.Such benches are constituted by the Chief Justice of India as required. Currently, there are 22 five-judge matters with 175 tagged matters pending in court.A permanent bench could make the process more predictable. Instead of repeatedly constituting a five-judge bench whenever a major constitutional question arises, a standing bench could hear such matters more continuously.It could also speed up constitutional litigation. Constitution Bench cases can remain pending for long periods because judges have multiple rosters and cases. A dedicated bench could potentially create greater continuity and reduce delays.A permanent bench could also bring greater consistency as the same group of judges will be dealing regularly with constitutional questions, which could develop continuity in constitutional jurisprudence, rather than different combinations of judges being assembled for different cases.It could also increase the importance of the CJI's roster decisions. The CJI is the master of the roster and decides which judges sit on particular benches. A permanent five-judge bench would therefore be a significant change in how the court allocates its most important constitutional cases.Constitution Benches decide some of the country's most consequential questions, including the limits of Parliament's power, fundamental rights, federalism, separation of powers and challenges to constitutional amendments.The Supreme Court has used Constitution Benches extensively in recent years; for example, 16 Constitution Bench judgments were delivered during former CJI D.Y. Chandrachud's tenure.
Article Summary: A two-judge SC bench has requested the CJI to explore setting up a permanent 5-Judge Constitutional Bench. Under Article 145(3), cases involving a "substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution" must be heard by at least five judges. A dedicated bench could potentially create greater continuity and reduce delays.

Article Title: Kalkaji gang-rape: Police probe if Aastha Kunj park was hunting ground of accused
Article Text:
The unlit road near LSR College where a police encounter with one of the accused took place Tuesda

Call detail records, CCTV footage place three accused near park at time of crime





NEW DELHI: Police investigating the alleged rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj park in south Delhi on Monday evening are trying to establish if the three accused have been involved in similar incidents earlier that have gone unreported.They were clearly looking for a vulnerable target, say police sources, with Asif - armed with a pistol and a condom in pocket - taking the lead in entering the park, followed by the two brothers, Hemant Singh and Mukesh Singh. They then teamed up to unleash 40 minutes of terror on the hapless couple.Police sources said the girl and her friend were sitting on a bench around 7:15 pm when the three men allegedly approached them, posing as policemen in civvies.Having intimidated the two teenagers, they took the boy around 200m away and slapped and threatened him before taking the girl to a secluded, dark stretch of the park. That's where they took turns to allegedly rape her. The girl was threatened against disclosing the incident to anyone.She was asked to leave the place immediately. By around 8pm, the men had left the spot, police said.According to the investigators, Hemant and Mukesh went out for dinner after that and returned home later. Asif seemed to be more cautious. Police got an early lead but couldn't find him either at the Okhla mandi or his house on Monday night.The girl returned to her friend and told him what had happened. The two left the park around 8:45pm. That's when the boy made a PCR call, which brought the cops to the park. The cops are now trying to establish how Asif had procured the pistol.They claim to have found "objectionable material", including videos, on Asif's phone, sources said. Some data was allegedly deleted from the phones of Hemant and Mukesh. These have been sent to Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) for retrieval.So far, the police have not come across any old complaints against the three. "We are checking whether someone may not have filed a complaint because of threats," a senior police officer said.The police are pursuing this angle because the three men would often hang around the park in the late hours. Hemant and Mukesh have allegedly changed their statements frequently during questioning. At one point, they claimed they were at home when the incident took place but gave a different account later. Their call detail records and CCTV footage, however, allegedly placed them near the park at the time.Sources said police are also investigating allegations that Hemant was removed from a gym he frequented following complaints of misbehaviour against him. The three have been sent to judicial custody for two days.DDA is facing a lot of flak for not having improved security in the park despite being alerted at least three times by the police since 2025. The police have pointed out that there were no CCTV cameras inside the park.Sources in DDA said their horticulture department had written multiple letters in the past one year to increase patrolling at the park. "Nine security guards are deployed in each shift at strategic locations, along with supervisory and patrolling arrangements. The lighting installations in the Aastha Kunj Park are functional and are inspected regularly. However, installing cameras at each spot won't be practical," a DDA official said.Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar, meanwhile, visited Aastha Kunj Park around 8.15pm Tuesday. He patrolled the park with other officers and reviewed security arrangements in and around the premises. He also directed the officers to further strengthen security through increased motorcycle and foot patrols .
Article Summary: Police trying to establish if the three accused have been involved in similar incidents earlier that have gone unreported. Asif - armed with a pistol and a condom in pocket - took the lead in entering the park. Hemant and Mukesh Singh then teamed up to unleash 40 minutes of terror on the couple.

Article Title: Roshibina Devi: From missing India's original squad to making history with silver, Roshibina Devi becomes first Indian woman to win three successive Asian Games medals
Article Text:
India's Roshibina Devi Naorem holds the silver medal after the Women's 60kg Wushu final match during the 20th Asian Games. (PTI Photo)

From controversy to the podium

Little time to prepare

India's Naorem Roshibina Devi, blue, competes against China's Zhang Xiaoyu in the in the Women's 60kg Wushu match final (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Naorem Roshibina Devi's Asian Games journey began with uncertainty but ended with another medal. The 25-year-old Manipuri wushu player won silver in the women's 60kg Sanda category after losing 0-2 to China's Zhang Xiaoyu in the final at the Aichi Prefectural Martial Arts Hall on Thursday.With the silver, Roshibina became the first Indian woman to win three successive Asian Games medals in wushu, following her bronze at Jakarta 2018 and silver at Hangzhou 2023.Roshibina was not part of India's original squad after losing the selection trial to Divyanshi Choudhary in June. Divyanshi was initially selected but was later withdrawn after the Wushu Association of India said an MRI showed a partial high-grade ACL tear.Divyanshi had alleged that she was being mentally and physically harassed and claimed Roshibina had been involved. The WAI rejected the allegations and said the squad change was made on medical grounds. The Sports Ministry subsequently approved Roshibina as the replacement.Roshibina, who learnt about her inclusion around September 10, said she wanted to move on from the controversy."What happened was not because of me. It was the federation's decision.Whatever decision the federation (Wushu Association of India) took, I think it was a good decision," she said."I will ignore it (the accusation). I just want to focus on my goal."Roshibina had been out of the national camp for around one-and-a-half months after losing the trials and travelled directly from Manipur after being recalled."There was a lot of disturbance when I came here for the Asian Games. I did not get much time to prepare. If I had more time, I would have done better," she said.Her coach Amit Pal also pointed to the lack of preparation, saying Roshibina had only limited training after being named in the team on September 10.Despite that, she defeated Bangladesh's Shika Khatun in the pre-quarterfinals and Macao, China's Chu Man Sin 5-0 in the quarterfinals before securing another Asian Games medal.Roshibina could not match Zhang's aggression and technical superiority in the gold-medal bout. The Chinese fighter won both rounds unanimously, with all five judges awarding her 5-0 decisions.Zhang dominated the scoring in both rounds, particularly with her side-kicks."She (Chinese player) is a new player, I have not fought against her. She was good in her side kicks. I also tried to defend. I tried to throw her, but she did better," Roshibina said.The silver left her disappointed at missing gold."I have won silver earlier and this time also, I could win only silver. I could not give the gold medal to the Indian people. I could not give what everyone wanted," she said.Born in Kwasiphai Mayai Leikai in Manipur's Bishnupur district, Roshibina's journey has also involved considerable family sacrifice, with her farmer father Naorem Damu Singh selling a piece of land to fund her training and travel in the early years.Now, with three successive Asian Games medals, Roshibina has another target."I want to inspire all the players. I want to be like them. I will do my best in the upcoming Games."
Article Summary: Naorem Roshibina Devi won silver in the women's 60kg Sanda category. She lost 0-2 to China's Zhang Xiaoyu in the final at the Aichi Prefectural Martial Arts Hall on Thursday. The 25-year-old Manipuri wushu player won bronze at Jakarta 2018 and silver at Hangzhou 2023.

Article Title: Chess Olympiad Round 7: India's chances of gold get bleaker despite win in open; women still in hunt
Article Text:
Nihal Sarin and Savitha Shri (Photo by Rafal Oleksiewicz and Michal Walusza for FIDE)

Savitha Shri , a potent force for India at 2026 Chess Olympiad

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India will look back at Nihal Sarin's loss before the rest day and wonder what might have happened had he taken a few more minutes — he had plenty of time on the clock, more than enough to have avoided the queen blunder that cost India their Round 6 match against Uzbekistan on Monday. When the players returned to the board for Round 7 in Samarkand on Wednesday, following Tuesday's rest day, the overall picture in the race for gold remained largely unchanged.Another hope of an Uzbek slip-up, this time at the hands of an in-form Chinese team, evaporated as the hosts won 3-1, moving a step closer to another coveted Chess Olympiad title. India's open team also won on the day, though not as comfortably as the Uzbeks.India's opponents were England, and with Dommaraju Gukesh and Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa having already wrapped up wins on their boards, the team's fate no longer rested on Nihal, which was just as well, because he lost again on Board 3, this time in a marathon 88-move battle against Luke McShane.McShane, playing white, produced a stubborn, fighting performance against the higher-rated Nihal.The Englishman took the initiative early, pushing pawns on both the queenside and kingside, while Nihal hit back with active piece play and a dangerous-looking attack on White's king.The position stayed unresolved for a long time, and by the time both players were down to their final seconds on the clock, the game had turned into a test of nerve as much as calculation.McShane held firm, found the right defensive moves under pressure, and gradually turned his rooks into the more active pieces on the board.The turning point came with 66.Re8, forcing off a pair of rooks and steering the game into a simplified endgame. This was exactly the kind of position where McShane's advanced f-pawn and increasingly active king took over.From there, he picked off Nihal's pawns one by one, and after nearly seven hours of play,Nihal resigned on move 88.It left Nihal with back-to-back individual losses at a tournament where he had otherwise been one of India's most reliable performers.India closed out the England match 2.5-1.5, with wins from Praggnanandhaa and Gukesh outweighing Nihal's loss and Arjun Erigaisi's draw.It keeps India firmly in the group chasing Uzbekistan, who remain the only team with a perfect record after seven rounds, a gap that will be hard to close with just four rounds left.If the open section's gold hopes are fading, India's women's team gave every reason to believe theirs are still very much alive, and 19-year-old Savitha Shri has been a big part of why.The Chennai-born player has now played six games at this Olympiad and won every single one, and Wednesday's win over Germany's Lara Schulze followed the same pattern.After a fairly balanced opening, Savitha. with the Whites, gradually seized control with active piece play and mounting pressure on the kingside.The position turned complicated around the 34th move, when she allowed a trade of pieces that led into a tricky rook-and-knight endgame, one she navigated calmly even as Schulze fell into serious time trouble.Savitha's rook grew increasingly active from there, picking off pawns and creating threats on both sides of the board, and though Schulze tried to fight back, Savitha never let her king come under real danger.In a phase that tested patience above all else, with both players short on time, Savitha pushed her kingside pawns forward until 88.g6+ proved decisive, leaving Schulze unable to save her rook.It capped a near-90-move grind with a well-earned win and helped India rout Germany 3.5-0.5, with Koneru Humpy and Divya Deshmukh also winning their games and Vaishali Rameshbabu drawing on Board 2.ALSO READ: Juggling Chess Olympiad prep and a commentary gig in India: The other side of USA's only female GM Irina Krush With India's open team hoping now for an unlikely Uzbek slip, they face Azerbaijan in Round 8 on Thursday. The women's team, who still hold better medal chances than their male counterparts on current form, take on Kazakhstan.
Article Summary: Savitha Shri has won all six games she has played at the 2026 Chess Olympiad. 19-year-old Chennai-born player beat Germany's Lara Schulze 3-5. India's open team also won on the day, though not as comfortably as the Uzbeks.

Article Title: Mirabai Chanu’s first coach sees another Olympic medal after elusive Asian Games silver
Article Text:
Mirabai Chanu during a training session ahead of the Asian Games and (pic right) with coach S Brojendro Singh after winning the gold medal at 2018 Commonwealth Games

TOI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

When a young Mirabai Chanu first walked into the weightlifting centre at Khuman Lampak in Imphal in 2006, there was little to suggest she would one day become India’s most decorated weightlifter.Twenty years later, after Mirabai clinched a silver medal in the women’s 49kg category at the Asian Games , her first-ever medal at the continental showpiece, her former coach S Brojendro Singh believes she is still not done.“I am very happy for her. She already has an Olympic medal, and I believe she will win another Olympic medal as well,” Singh told. “Now that she has won an Asian Games medal, I believe she can win a medal in Los Angeles, too.”Singh coached Mirabai at the state sports academy at Khuman Lampak Main Stadium from 2006 to 2011, overseeing the now 32-year-old lifter’s formative years in the sport. Those early days, he recalled, were marked by a work ethic that set her apart from her peers.“Whatever she was told to do, she did it. She never missed any instruction. If we asked her to do something, she would complete it exactly as told,” said Singh, who has been coaching at the academy since 2004.“That discipline was different. She was also fearless and never shied away from a challenge.”Not everything was smooth at the beginning. Singh remembered a period when the youngster stopped attending training sessions.“She was absent for almost a month early in 2007. I got worried and went straight to her home. Later, I found out that she had chickenpox. Once she recovered, she returned and continued training,” said the coach, who has trained numerous other international medallists, including Rishikanta Singh and Nirupama Devi.Asked if he had spotted signs of greatness in the teenager, Singh pointed not to extraordinary physical attributes but to her attitude. “Her dedication was exceptional. She listened, she worked hard and she was never afraid. Those qualities made her different from the others,” he said.Mirabai’s rise from Khuman Lampak to the Olympic podium has also inspired a generation of weightlifters in Manipur, but Singh believes athletes with her combination of talent, discipline and determination are rare.“In all my years as a coach, I have not seen another weightlifter quite like Mirabai,” he said. “Many athletes look up to her, but finding someone with her qualities is very difficult.”Having won Olympic silver in Tokyo and now added an elusive Asian Games medal to her collection, after also securing her third Commonwealth Games gold medal, Mirabai may have achieved almost everything in the sport. Yet, if her first coach is to be believed, the story is far from over.“She still has a lot to achieve,” Singh said. “I am confident there is more to come from her.”Long before the Olympic medal, the world title and the Asian Games silver, Mirabai’s days revolved around hitching rides on passing trucks to travel from her village to Imphal for training and helping her family by collecting firewood and carrying water uphill in the hills of Manipur.Two decades on, the resilience forged during those years continues to power one of India’s greatest sporting careers and, if her first coach is right, perhaps another Olympic medal run as well.
Article Summary: Mirabai Chanu won silver in the women's 49kg category at the Asian Games. Her first-ever medal at the continental showpiece. Her former coach S Brojendro Singh believes she is still not done. Singh coached Mirabai at the state sports academy at Khuman Lampak.

Article Title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez bought a €25 million plot on Dubai’s ‘Billionaire Island’ to build a custom mansion, after leasing their Madrid villa for €10,000 a month
Article Text:
Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez bought a €25 million plot on Dubai’s ‘Billionaire Island’ to build a custom mansion, after leasing their Madrid villa for €10,000 a month

What Was The Valuation Behind Cristiano Ronaldo And Georgina Rodríguez’s €25 Million Jumeirah Bay Land Deal

What Features Define The Custom Megamansion Development For Cristiano Ronaldo And Georgina Rodríguez

How Did Georgina Rodríguez’s Madrid Memories Show The Scale Of Cristiano Ronaldo’s La Finca Home

I Am Georgina

Why Did Cristiano Ronaldo And Georgina Rodríguez Lease Their Madrid Villa For €10,000 A Month

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez expanded their property portfolio in 2024 with a €25 million land purchase on Dubai’s Jumeirah Bay Island, a luxury development often called “Billionaire Island”. The couple planned to build a private mansion on the waterfront plot as Ronaldo continued his career with Saudi Pro League club Al-Nassr. The purchase came after they had put their Madrid home in La Finca up for rent for €10,000 a month in 2023. The Dubai deal gave the family a permanent property base in the Gulf while adding another major asset to Ronaldo’s international real estate portfolio.Ronaldo and Rodríguez reportedly paid €25 million (£21 million/$27 million) for the Dubai plot in 2024. The land is on Jumeirah Bay Island, a man-made island shaped roughly like a seahorse and located off Dubai’s coast.The island is known for its small number of high-end homes and its location close to some of Dubai’s luxury hotels and facilities. It is connected to the mainland by a private bridge and is home to the Bulgari Resort and Bulgari Yacht Club.ge.globo reported in June 2024 that the couple had completed the purchase and planned to build a mansion for themselves and their five children.The report said the property was expected to be ready by the end of December that year.The purchase also made sense geographically for Ronaldo. His professional life had moved to Saudi Arabia after joining Al-Nassr, while Dubai offered a nearby base for the family and their wider business interests.The island’s appeal is not simply its location. Jumeirah Bay Island has become one of Dubai’s most exclusive residential areas, with a limited number of waterfront properties. Khaleej Times reported that the island has 124 sea-facing villas across the development, highlighting how limited the residential supply is.Instead of purchasing a finished house, Ronaldo and Rodríguez planned a home around their own requirements. Reports in 2024 linked the project to Palace Luxury Living, a UAE luxury property company.The biggest difference is that the Dubai home was planned as a private family residence rather than simply another investment property. Ronaldo and Rodríguez have five children, so the layout needed to work for a large family as well as their staff.Details reported about the planned property have included large living areas, private bedrooms, fitness facilities and outdoor spaces facing the water. The waterfront setting also gives the family direct access to the Dubai coastline.Rodríguez has also shown a strong interest in the design of the couple’s homes. Their previous residences have featured modern interiors, large open areas, marble surfaces and extensive outdoor spaces.That approach is easy to understand when looking at the size of the family’s other homes. Ronaldo’s properties have often been designed around football, fitness, privacy and family life rather than simply being luxury addresses.The Dubai mansion therefore fits into a pattern already seen across the couple’s property portfolio: large spaces, private facilities and enough room for family life without giving up the features expected from a high-end home.Long before Dubai became part of their property story, Rodríguez had already experienced what it was like to live in one of Ronaldo’s unusually large homes.The couple’s Madrid residence is located in La Finca, an exclusive residential development in Pozuelo de Alarcón. Ronaldo bought the property in 2010 for around €5 million while he was playing for Real Madrid.The home later became closely associated with Rodríguez through her Netflix series. When she first moved into Ronaldo’s home, she admitted that its size made it difficult for her to find her way around.“The first time I came to Cristiano’s house, well I’d get lost,” Rodríguez revealed in her hit Netflix docuseries I Am Georgina. “I’d want to go to the kitchen to get water and I’d no idea where to go. Sometimes it would take me half an hour to get to the living room because I didn’t know the way back. Since I was a kid I had been so used to living in really small apartments”.She later said it took about six months before she knew the house properly.The Madrid property was designed by architect Joaquín Torres and has been reported as having seven bedrooms and nine bathrooms, along with indoor and outdoor pools and a gym. Ronaldo also added personal touches, including CR7-branded door handles.The scale of the property became even more notable after the couple decided they no longer needed to keep it solely as their family home.After Ronaldo left Real Madrid and later moved through Juventus and Manchester United before joining Al-Nassr, his time in Madrid became much more limited. In 2023, the couple put the La Finca property on the rental market for €10,000 a month.La Vanguardia reported that the house had been Ronaldo’s Madrid home during his Real Madrid years and was later offered for rent at that monthly price. The report also noted that the property was offered furnished.The decision meant the couple could keep the Madrid property instead of selling it while no longer using it as their main home.Reports described the residence as a large multi-level property with several bedrooms, bathrooms, a gym and swimming pools. Much of the furniture and decoration stayed in the house, allowing a tenant to move into the property without having to furnish it from scratch.The Dubai purchase then added a very different kind of property to their portfolio. Madrid represented Ronaldo’s long connection with Spain and his Real Madrid years. Article Title: In 2024, a 57-year-old man ran from Cape Town to Cairo in 301 days; gunmen in Ethiopia nearly kidnapped him during his 6,706-mile long journey
Article Text:
Keith Boyd completed a 6,706-mile journey from Cape Town to Cairo in 301 days in 2024, setting a new record for the fastest journey between the two cities on foot. Image Credit: GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS

How did a 57-year-old run from Cape Town to Cairo

Image Credit: GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS

The daily running routine behind Boyd’s record-breaking journey

Image Credit: GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS

How did the Ethiopia kidnapping attempt change the journey

The final Ethiopian section brought further danger

Why did Boyd take on such a demanding challenge

The run took a heavy physical toll

Keith Boyd completed a 6,706-mile journey from Cape Town to Cairo in 301 days in 2024, setting a new record for the fastest journey between the two cities on foot. The 57-year-old British-South African runner crossed 9 countries during the challenge, but the route became particularly dangerous in Ethiopia, where he and his videographer were stopped, beaten and held by armed men. Despite the serious security problems, Boyd eventually completed the remaining section of his route and reached Cairo, surpassing the previous record by 17 days.Boyd covered 10,793 kilometres, travelling through South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Tanzania, Kenya, Ethiopia, Sudan and Egypt. Guinness World Records reported that he completed the journey in 301 days, beating a 25-year-old record of 318 days by 17 days. Men's Fitness reported his exact finishing time as 301 days, 20 hours and 58 minutes, with Boyd reaching Cairo on 22 May 2024.The route was not simply a continuous run from one capital to another. Boyd had to change his plans because of the conflict in Sudan. He had originally intended to travel in the opposite direction, from Cairo to Cape Town, but chose to begin in South Africa in the hope that conditions in Sudan would improve by the time he reached that country.The journey was supported by a small team travelling in a van carrying camping equipment and medical supplies.During the earlier stages, Boyd made steady progress. Guinness World Records reported that he crossed South Africa in 47 days, while Botswana and Zimbabwe took a little over two weeks. Zambia, Tanzania and Kenya each took roughly a month.Boyd averaged around 50 kilometres a day during much of the challenge, often dividing the distance into five 10-kilometre sections. As reported by Men's Fitness, he described a slightly different routine during the Sudan and Egypt sections, when he normally began around 5.30am and ran four blocks of about 12.5 kilometres, walking for 20 to 30 minutes between them.Not every day followed the same pattern. Some days involved as little as 5 kilometres, while others reached 50 kilometres. Overall, Men's Fitness reported 125 days as his longest continuous stretch of back-to-back running. It also reported 60 non-running days, including 54 linked to Ethiopian security and paperwork problems, five because of illness and one for repacking.Preparation for such a long journey was intensive. Guinness World Records reported that Boyd trained for 4 months, running about 200 kilometres each week to build strength and endurance in his feet, legs and back.Ethiopia became the most dangerous part of the expedition. Boyd was travelling through the northern Amhara region when he and his videographer were stopped by armed men. According to Guinness World Records, the pair were beaten and forced into a van after being intercepted while trying to cross the area.Men's Fitness reported that the gunmen demanded his support team to arrange for a ransom. He and the videographer were threatened with being taken into a forest, where finding them would have been extremely difficult. Boyd managed to delay the situation and eventually negotiated their release for $1,000.Afterwards, he continued for another 100 kilometres with a military escort. The security situation eventually became too dangerous, however, and he had to leave Ethiopia and continue towards Sudan without completing that section.The experience meant that reaching Cairo did not immediately mark the end of the challenge. Boyd still had approximately 500 kilometres of Ethiopia to complete.After reaching Cairo, Boyd sought permission and security assistance to return to Ethiopia and finish the missing section. Guinness World Records reported that he petitioned the Ethiopian government for protection but received no response for almost three weeks. He eventually arranged the journey with local civilians and officials.The return was still extremely difficult. Guinness World Records reported that Boyd and his team were ambushed and had to take cover in a ditch. They were also held overnight in an overcrowded cell without being charged and faced further threats and assaults from armed men. Despite those setbacks, he completed the final stretch and left the region safely.The run had a purpose beyond the record. Guinness World Records reported that Boyd undertook the challenge to raise money for Rainbow Leaders, his non-profit organisation, which works to encourage young people in Africa to participate in elections as part of efforts to address poverty.Boyd had also spent more than 30 years working in telecommunications in Africa, giving him a long personal connection with the continent and its communities. The challenge therefore combined an endurance goal with fundraising and civic engagement.The distance and length of the journey placed considerable strain on Boyd's body. Men's Fitness reported that his feet and particularly his left ankle became swollen, while he also developed tendonitis. He used 3 types of running shoes to deal with different problems, including ankle stability, impact and rough terrain.Recovery became part of his daily routine. Boyd said he aimed for 8 to 9 hours of sleep and used stretching and a roller to help his body recover. He also consumed protein through shakes and bars, although he lost weight and muscle from his thighs during the journey.
Article Summary: Keith Boyd completed a 6,706-mile journey from Cape Town to Cairo in 301 days in 2024. The 57-year-old British-South African runner crossed 9 countries during the challenge. The route became particularly dangerous in Ethiopia, where he and his videographer were stopped, beaten and held by armed men. Despite the serious security problems, Boyd eventually completed the remaining section of his route and reached Cairo.
