Article Title: Unplayed Mongolia fixture denies India shot at historic Asian Games esports medal
Article Text:
India eye record medals at Asian Games 2026

New Delhi:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s hopes of securing a historic esports medal at the Asian Games in Japan suffered a setback after an unplayed eFootball fixture against Mongolia was recorded as a forfeit win, leaving India without the goal difference it needed to remain in contention for the knockout stage.India’s eFootball pair of Chinmay Sahoo and Danial Patel, coached by Saksham Rattan, had earlier drawn 0-0 against Uzbekistan’s Abubakir Iminjonov and Farrukh Mirkhamitov. With India needing a win in its next Group F fixture, Mongolia’s Munkh-Ochir Batmanlai and Khantamir Munkh-Orgil failed to report to the Call Room within the stipulated time. India was subsequently awarded a 0-0 forfeit victory.However, Uzbekistan defeated Mongolia 2-0 across the console and mobile matches and finished top of Group F. With only the group winner advancing directly to the quarterfinals, India’s campaign ended despite its awarded victory.The Esports Federation of India (ESFI) has raised concerns over the circumstances surrounding the fixture and the subsequent qualification calculations. The federation said India was denied the opportunity to actually play Mongolia, score goals and improve its goal difference, which it says was relevant to determining qualification among the teams.According to ESFI, Uzbekistan was able to play its fixture against Mongolia and subsequently benefited from the resulting goal difference before eventually winning the bronze medal. ESFI has questioned whether recording no goal difference for India’s forfeited match created an unequal sporting opportunity.The federation also cited a series of technical and scheduling disruptions. Matches scheduled for 9am reportedly began only after 11.30am due to problems with an organiser-provided playing device. The Uzbekistan-Mongolia fixture, scheduled for around 3pm, reportedly started at approximately 5pm Japan time, affecting the timing of the India-Mongolia encounter.ESFI further alleged that Mongolia had not been adequately briefed about the required Call Room reporting time and that its team manager was unable to leave the preceding match to complete the reporting process for the next fixture.The federation said India’s subsequent request for a review by the Olympic Council of Asia, the Esports Organising Committee and competition management went unacknowledged. ESFI also alleged that India was not given adequate clarity on the applicable rules within the stipulated 15-minute window to lodge a formal protest.India sought clarification on the regulatory basis for recording no goal difference in forfeited matches, the use of average points and average goal difference for ranking, the complete qualification calculations and when the ranking methodology was formally communicated to participating teams.ESFI has called for a transparent review, a written response and appropriate corrective action, while reaffirming its respect for competition rules and technical officials.India’s 15-member esports contingent is competing across four disciplines: eFootball, Puyo Puyo Champions, Pokémon UNITE and League of Legends.
Article Summary: India’s hopes of securing a historic esports medal at the Asian Games suffered a setback. An unplayed eFootball fixture against Mongolia was recorded as a forfeit win, leaving India without the goal difference it needed to remain in contention for the knockout stage. Uzbekistan defeated Mongolia 2-0 across the console and mobile matches and finished top of Group F.

Article Title: From missing Hangzhou to silver in Nagoya: Mirabai Chanu’s Asian Games redemption
Article Text:
Mirabai Chanu (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nagoya: Two hundred and sixty-four grams.That was all it took to complete Mirabai Chanu ’s collection of heavyweight medals.The silver medallion awarded at Aichi-Nagoya weighs 264gm, but for Mirabai it could well be worth its weight in gold.Six years ago, it was also in Japan that Mirabai won an Olympic silver at the Tokyo Games. In the land of the rising sun, she delivered again, this time in a statement of persistence and resilience.At the Nagoya City Trade and Industry Centre here on Wednesday, the 32-year-old ended India’s 28-year wait for an Asian Games weightlifting medal, winning silver and, in the process, finally adding a continental medal to her cabinet.“I feel very good. This Asian Games medal was my dream and finally I got a silver medal. Since I stepped into the elite level, this has been my dream,” gushed Mirabai after her medal-winning performance.Competing in the 49kg category, the lifter, who wore tricolour hair ties, totalled 198kg (87kg in snatch + 111kg in clean and jerk) to finish behind defending champion Ri Song-gum. The North Korean was in another stratosphere altogether, lifting a world-record 215kg (94+121), a full 17kg more than the Indian.Indonesia’s Luluk Diana Tri Wijayana took bronze with 191kg (88+103).Mirabai was assured in the snatch, clearing 83kg, 85kg and 87kg without much fuss. She trailed Ri and Luluk going into the clean and jerk, but successfully negotiated 107kg and 111kg to secure silver.Asked why the continental medal was her dream and not the Olympic silverware which she already possessed, Mirabai said, “Competition in Asian weightlifting is very strong with Korea, China etc. I believe that medals in Asian Games are equal to the ones won at the Olympics. In fact, I feel the competition at the Asian Games is tougher than the Olympics.”For an athlete who had dreamed of an Asian Games podium for years, the medal was also a measure of redemption.Mirabai missed the 2018 edition because of a back injury. In Hangzhou three years ago, a hip and thigh injury hampered her during her final attempt and left her fourth.Earlier this year, a lingering shoulder injury had cast another shadow over her season. But Mirabai put that behind her by winning gold at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games.Her resilience has deep roots.Born in Nongpok Kakching in southeastern Manipur, Mirabai grew up in a landscape that is picturesque and also steeped in history and identity. The region, known for landmarks such as Kakching Garden and the People’s Museum, has also witnessed the imprint of World War II, with Langol Peak serving as a campsite for Allied forces. From that landscape emerged an athlete who has repeatedly had to rise after setbacks.If age and injuries threatened to slow her down, Mirabai had a support system that refused to let that happen. While coach Vijay Sharma took care of her training, American strength and conditioning coach Dr Aaron Horschig monitored her fitness and recovery. A nutritionist, meanwhile, ensured she stayed on top of her weight.The work that went into the medal, she said, was immense.“A lot of work. After the Commonwealth Games, there was very little time. At the same time, I had to control my weight at 48kg (for the CWG). It was very difficult for me to control my weight,” explained the Padma Shri awardee.One of the most keenly watched Indian athletes at the Games, Mirabai also had to contend with the weight of expectation.“There is pressure, but I also have confidence. The whole world has had hopes of me winning a medal. I draw strength from the fact that people think positively about me and pray for me so much. That said, the pressure of not delivering is also there,” she said.With the Asian Games medal finally ticked off her bucket list, attention inevitably turns to another question: is a fourth Olympic appearance at the 2028 Los Angeles Games on the horizon?“We haven’t finalised anything yet. But we will try. Qualifying starts in Dec. But for now, I will enjoy it,” she signed off.
Article Summary: Mirabai Chanu won silver in the 49kg category at the Asian Games. The 32-year- old ended India’s 28-year wait for an Asian Games medal. She finished behind defending champion Ri Song-gum of North Korea.

Article Title: Dangers unseen: Unprotected and unlit, Delhi parks fail safety tests after dark
Article Text:
The conditions assume significance after the alleged gang rape of a minor at Aastha Kunj Park brought safety inside the capital’s green spaces into focus

Delhi parks fail safety tests

MAZE OF UNLIT TRAILS

WHEN PHONE FLASHLIGHT IS A MUST

TRESPASSERS FOX GUARDS

NEITHER BLEAK NOR PERFECT





A well-lit pathway can give way to darkness within a few turns. A guarded entrance at one end may be undone by an unmanned gate at another. Across some of Delhi’s sprawling parks, lighting, visibility and security change sharply from one stretch to the next, leaving secluded pockets within otherwise busy public spaces.The conditions assume significance after the alleged gang rape of a minor at Aastha Kunj Park brought safety inside the capital’s green spaces into focus. TOI visits some of them.At Buddha Jayanti Park in Central Ridge, a few steps are enough to move from a manicured pathway into a maze of overgrown tracks. Gate No. 2 was still open at 6pm. Cars could drive into the parking area, but there was no guard stationed at the entrance. From there, a lane on the left stretched towards the canteen. This was groomed, easy to follow and lined with lamp posts, though the lights had not been switched on as the park neared its closing time.But take the tracks to the right, and the setting changes abruptly. Narrow trails disappeared into thick, unkempt vegetation, some seemingly running endlessly into the bushes. At places, shrubs hung so low over the tracks that one had to stoop to pass.Unlike the peripheral path, where lamp posts stood roughly 50 metres apart, several of these inner tracks had no visible lighting at all. There were few people around: a family of three, a few couples and a biker. “I have a field job and there is no entry fee here, so I came to the park to rest,” the biker said.According to the timings displayed on a board, the park remains open from 5am to 7pm between April 1 and Sept 30, and 6am to 6pm from Oct 1 to March 31. At 6.15pm, toilets were being locked, and people were asked to leave the park. Yet, with the entrance unguarded and several secluded tracks cutting through the vegetation, monitoring who remained inside appeared to rest largely on a final sweep of the grounds.A guard in civilian clothes, carrying a stick, was seen telling visitors to leave. “I check the whole park to make sure everyone has left. Then I lock it,” he said. “Four people are there to look after it, but the others have gone to their villages. So, I am the only one here. I have already locked one gate at 6pm. Now I have to lock the other.”In 2003, a 17-year-old DU student was raped by two members of the President’s Bodyguard inside this park. Four personnel were ultimately convicted. In 2010, two drivers associated with Delhi Police were arrested for allegedly attempting to rape a woman and assaulting her companion inside the park.The phone flashlight comes out before the evening walk is over. At several points inside Rohini’s Swarn Jayanti Park, visitors use it to find their way through the darkness. For a park’s safety check, it’s an immediate red flag. Spread across 170 acres, Japanese Park, as it is popularly known, has gardens, boating areas and picnic spots. The crowds and lights at the entrance can make it feel alive. However, the deeper one goes, the harder it is to spot a guard or even another visitor.In 2013, a businessman’s body with his throat slit was found in a lake inside the park, after which the park was reportedly shut before reopening in 2015. In 2017, two 19-year-old cousins were chased and stabbed to death inside the park. In Jan 2026, an 18-year-old was stabbed to death.A recent spot check found a guard at Gate 1 near the parking area, but little security was visible inside. At several points, visitors used phone flashlights to walk. The closing time appeared another grey area. Some said it is 7.30pm, others 8pm. Yet people remained inside beyond these timings. Google lists it as open till 11pm. Given the park’s size and dense stretches, someone venturing too deep could even struggle to find his way back. Tushali, a resident from a nearby area, said she avoids going deep after dark. Sima, a regular visitor, said she knows which areas to avoid and claimed couples, gamblers and smokers gather deeper inside. Anushka, visiting with her husband, said she felt fine when accompanied but found the isolated stretches uncomfortable when alone.At Vijay Mandal Park in Begumpur, a short walk from Sri Aurobindo College, the evening deadline appeared to mark the end of official access, but not necessarily of movement into the park. The green space, frequented by walkers and college students during the day, was dimly lit as darkness set in. Lamp posts were there, but dark pockets still existed as some people walked and jogged around. One woman had her phone flashlight on. A board at the entrance listed the park’s timings as 5am to 8pm.At 8pm, two guards shut the main gate, stopping people from entering and asking those inside to leave. Yet, two people could be seen scaling the iron grille along the park’s boundary and jumping inside at that very moment.A guard stationed at the entrance said there is another gate on the opposite side of the park. “But we aren’t sure if that gate is still open or whether the guards on that side will man it after 8pm,” he said. Some students said poor lighting added to their unease. “Trespassers are common. For women, it’s not safe. There should be more lighting,” said Manish, a second-year Sri Aurobindo College student. Himani, another second-year student, said she avoids the park after sunset. Some visitors alleged that people entered the park just to consume drugs.A Congress worker was beaten and shot dead while taking a morning walk in this park last year, while in 2023, a woman was hit with an iron rod and killed in broad daylight.Sheesh Mahal Park in Shalimar Bagh presents a mixed picture. The DDAmanaged park is mostly well lit with guard rooms at several points. But its quiet, secluded stretches have witnessed serious crime.In 2017, a 16-year-old girl was gang-raped inside the park, while her male friend was assaulted and robbed. The case exposed the park’s dark patches at that time — from faulty high-mast lights, broken boundary walls (now, there’s a grille) and a shortage of guards. In Aug 2023, a labourer was found dead inside the park, with police registering a case of murder.At the entrance, a board called it a “family park” and warned against “indecent activities”. As the sun set and the crowd thinned, much of the park remained lit. But deep inside, several lights were not working, and dark patches appeared here and there. Urmila, returning from work, said she avoids the quieter stretches because the lights are often on the blink.Dinesh Sharma, who was with his daughter, said things were different three to four years ago, when gamblers used to frequent the park. Since exArmy personnel became guards, things are “way better”, he claimed.TOI found seven to eight guards stationed at one point, who said they patrol the park. Still, the dark stretches remained. For visitors, the equation is simple: guards help, but a faulty light or two can still turn a lush patch into a blind spot.
Article Summary: The conditions assume significance after the alleged gang rape of a minor at Aastha Kunj Park. At Buddha Jayanti Park in Central Ridge, a few steps are enough to move from a manicured pathway into a maze of overgrown tracks. The deeper one goes, the harder it is to spot a guard or even another visitor.

Article Title: ‘Doctors removed both eyes’: School skit on mobile use leaves students crying
Article Text:
Khatima block education officer Bhanu Pratap Kushwaha said the method was inappropriate





RUDRAPUR: An awareness programme aimed at discouraging excessive mobile phone use left several students frightened and in tears at a private school in Khatima, prompting education officials to issue a notice to the institution.The incident took place at Montessori Indian Public School in Biriya Majhola village of Udham Singh Nagar district. A video of the programme, showing students distressed during a staged act depicting the effects of excessive screen use, has circulated widely on social media.The school organised the programme after parents and villagers raised concerns about children spending increasing amounts of time on mobile phones and other screens. Local social worker Kamal Singh said villagers had approached principal Hema Chufal, seeking measures to make students aware of the possible harmful effects of excessive phone use.Students dressed as doctors and patients enacted scenes depicting the alleged effects of prolonged screen time on eyesight and mental well-being. The portrayal took a disturbing turn when a child playing a patient claimed excessive mobile phone use had resulted in doctors removing both his eyes.His eyes were covered with bandages and red-coloured material was applied around them.The enactment frightened his classmates, with some screaming and crying after apparently believing their friend had actually been injured. The video shows the children visibly distressed before they took a pledge to reduce or stop excessive mobile phone use.Chufal said she had initially been apprehensive about the impact of the act but claimed parents later appreciated its message. “Initially, I was worried that the play might have a negative impact on the children. But when they returned home and asked their parents not to let them use mobile phones excessively, the parents were satisfied,” she said.Khatima block education officer Bhanu Pratap Kushwaha said the method was inappropriate. “The way the children were sensitised about excessive mobile phone use and screen time was not right. It created panic among them. A notice has been issued to the school in this regard,” he said.Khatima block education officer Bhanu Pratap Kushwaha said the method was inappropriate. “The way the children were sensitised about excessive mobile phone use and screen time was not right. It created panic among them. A notice has been issued to the school in this regard,” he said.

Article Title: Anthropic’s Claude AI discovers new enzyme system in bacteria-infecting viruses; Dario Amodei says: We believe AI for biology is on a similar...
Article Text:
Claude spotted a CRISPR-like pattern that earlier studies missed

Around 950 Claude agents searched DNA data for 21 hours

CRISPR pioneer Feng Zhang calls the finding worth a closer look

Dario Amodei says AI in biology is on the same curve as maths

Anthropic says its Claude AI has found a previously unknown enzyme system inside viruses that infect bacteria, and its layout looks a lot like CRISPR, the natural machinery behind the world's best-known gene editing tool. The company has named it array-associated reverse transcriptase, or ART, and says Claude did most of the work after its scientists gave it a single broad prompt.The finding is the first result from Anthropic's new life sciences research group and wet lab, set up in the Bay Area this spring. What ART does is still unknown. CEO Dario Amodei said as much in a post on X, noting that its precise function, biotech usefulness "(if any)" and significance are not yet clear. "But at minimum it is work I would have been proud to do as a PhD student," he wrote.ART has three parts. There is a reverse transcriptase (RT), an enzyme that copies RNA into DNA. There is a partner gene of unknown function sitting beside it. And there is a long array of evenly spaced DNA repeats.That repeat array is what invites the CRISPR comparison. In CRISPR systems, a similar array stores a bank of RNA sequences, which is what makes them programmable.The RT itself, found in a jumbo phage, had been identified in earlier research. Anthropic says Claude appears to be the first to notice the array and the accessory protein around it. Early lab tests show the array is expressed as a set of distinct short RNAs, which suggests ART may work in a way similar to CRISPR. Experiments to confirm its function are ongoing, and a pre-print is already out.Anthropic says roughly 950 Claude agents spent 21 hours combing through a massive database of DNA sequences, using 210 million tokens along the way. They gathered more than 200,000 RTs, shortlisted 3,500 new candidate systems and narrowed those to 20, each with a report written for human review. The company says this kind of analysis can take an expert scientist weeks to months.The moment of discovery came while one agent was reading raw DNA next to an odd-looking RT. Its note read: "that's a CRISPR-like … repeat array?!" It then counted the repeats, measured their spacing, compared the layout with known RT systems and checked the literature before flagging it.Amodei described the split carefully. The work was done "mostly, though not entirely, by Claude," he wrote. The team picked the research area, Claude read the literature and genome data and proposed experiments, and human scientists ran them. The lab only handles biosafety level 1 and 2 work, with no pathogens that infect people, and the team used Claude Science and Claude Code, the same tools any scientist can access.Feng Zhang, one of the pioneers of CRISPR genome editing and a professor at MIT and the Broad Institute, reviewed the pre-print. He called it "an exciting example of how AI agents can contribute to biological discovery" and said the RNA-repeat arrays were "intriguing and merits further investigation."Amodei also pointed out that a Stanford team, working separately, recently described a different RT system with a similar array. The two evolved independently, he said.Amodei used the announcement to make a wider case. In 2023, he wrote, AI models struggled with high-school maths. By late 2026, they are beginning to solve some of the hardest open problems in the field. He believes biology is on a similar exponential trend.Biology, of course, needs lab work. Amodei says humans working with AI can validate key results in a few weeks, and that Claude may one day run lab equipment itself with safeguards in place, though Anthropic isn't doing that yet.He was clear that faster discovery won't shorten clinical trials. It could, however, send many more promising drug candidates into the pipeline. That links back to his 2024 essay Machines of Loving Grace, where he wrote that AI could help "cure most diseases in 5-10 years."Anthropic now plans to expand its life sciences team and is inviting outside scientists to pitch collaborations. Whether ART ever becomes a tool on the scale of CRISPR is anyone's guess. What Anthropic has shown is that Claude can find something in public DNA data that had been sitting there, unnoticed, until now.
Article Summary: Anthropic says its Claude AI has found a previously unknown enzyme system inside viruses that infect bacteria. Its layout looks a lot like CRISPR, the natural machinery behind the world's best-known gene editing tool. The company has named it array-associated reverse transcriptase, or ART. What ART does is still unknown.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on AI doomsday warnings from Dario Amodei, Sam Altman and others: Don’t think for a second just because you’re …
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

Jensen Huang: All of Geoffrey Hinton’s predictions are wrong

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang pushed back against warnings from some of the biggest names in the AI world that AI could eventually become uncontrollable and threaten humanity. In an interview on The Ezra Klein Show recently, Jensen Huang was asked about concerns raised by AI pioneers including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , Geoffrey Hinton as well as Ilya Sutskever. Huang said such warnings should be based on evidence and science, arguing that alarming people about AI does not automatically serve a “social good”.“Don’t think for a second just because you’re an alarmist that you’re doing a social good. It is not true,” Huang said adding “I think that we ought to just all be wiser, more mature, be evidence based, be scientific”.“If you want to be scientific, be scientific. Do the science. But alarming people, making claims that don’t — their track record is horrible. Their track record is literally horrible,” he stated.During the podcast, Huang was asked whether he believed Geoffrey Hinton’s warnings that a “10 percent chance of societal destruction (because of AI) is not unreasonable”. The Nvidia chief responded saying:“I would tell Geoff that it’s irresponsible to say all that. All of his predictions have been wrong. Enough predictions. That 10 percent chance is not grounded on science. It’s not grounded on research. Just because it comes from a scientist doesn’t make it scientific. Those predictions are hurtful”.Earlier this year, Geoffrey Hinton, popularly called Godfather of AI said that people should stop training radiologists, adding that within 5 years, deep learning is going to do better than radiologists.“Let’s take it at face value that the recommendation is exactly what he said, which is that nobody should want to be a radiologist and the world has no radiologists today,” Huang said.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang: All of Geoffrey Hinton’s predictions have been wrong. Huang said such warnings should be based on evidence and science. Huang argued that alarming people about AI does not automatically serve a “social good”.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: A 25-year-old techie fell into a trap by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram. Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal's combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026.

Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: Theatre review: A playful, if uneven, take on the Jane Austen classic
Article Text:
A still from the play

Pride and Prejudice

Fly Me to the Moon

Flowers

I Wanna Hold Your Hand

Want us to review your play? Mail us at tims.delhitimes@timesofindia.com





It is a truth universally acknowledged that not every adaptation of a classic can live up to the expectations attached to it. A recent musical adaptation of Jane Austen’sby the Theatre For A Cause (TFAC) group succeeds, albeit in parts.The opening sequence sees Elizabeth Bennet dancing gaily with her father, Mr Bennet, to a rather lovely rendition of Bart Howard’s. Enter Mrs Bennet, announcing that a ball is to take place in honour of Mr Bingley and his team’s arrival. Almost immediately, Mrs Bennet thinks that her elder daughter Jane should present herself as a prospective match. And so the ten steps of a Victorian courtship that ultimately leads to a union begins.Dramatic and borderline greedy – actor Pratibha’s version of the annoying Mrs Bennet is a delight. From almost fainting at every new piece of information, to her bluntness of speech; the tiniest nuance of the character is embodied with utmost sincerity. Her comic timing brings a novel energy to a story that is over 200 years old.One could very well ask, what could be so exciting about a narrative that has been retold so many times over the years?TFAC’s play works as a playful musical. But these interventions also somehow interrupt its flow.While the dancers bring a certain vigour to Austen’s familiar world, the performances also feel like individual set pieces instead of being part of a cohesive whole.As the lights shine and dancers begin throwing graceful shapes on the floor, Bingley leaves town without anything but a letter to Jane. A singer begins singing Miley Cyrus’, the Grammy-winning song on self-love. Suddenly, one could feel the entire mood of the auditorium shift, shoulders swaying to the beats as some even sing along to the lyrics.But Jane feeling spurned and then embodying self-love feels like an awkward sidenote which is never addressed. The song works emotionally on its own, but feels disconnected from Jane’s journey.One of the most interesting segments apart from the musical elements is Wickham’s dramatic entry. Wickham’s regiment makes its way through the audience, catching everyone by surprise. It is one of the moments where the theatricality works particularly well, using the space rather than simply presenting another musical number.The production has winning moments, especially the bits where it doesn’t take itself too seriously. The singers, dancers and the actors playing Mr, Mrs Bennet and Mr Bingley add life to an all too familiar tale.However, the proposal ultimately worded by Mr Darcy to Lizzy leaves an odd aftertaste as it cuts abruptly and concludes on The Beatles’-Anvita Singh
Article Summary: A recent musical adaptation of Jane Austen’s Pride and Prejudice by the Theatre For A Cause (TFAC) group succeeds, albeit in parts. The production has winning moments, especially the bits where it doesn’t take itself too seriously. However, the proposal ultimately worded by Mr Darcy to Lizzy leaves an odd aftertaste.

Article Title: Theatre Review: A love story that reaches beyond romance
Article Text:
Ek Lamhaa Zindagi is a captivating biographical play that delves into the lives of renowned writers Razia Sajjad Zaheer and Sajjad Zaheer. Starring Juhi Babbar Soni, who masterfully embodies various roles, the narrative intertwines the couple's dynamic relationship with pivotal historical moments, such as the freedom struggle and India’s Independence. This performance, hosted at Prithvi Theatre, artfully weaves personal experiences with significant historical developments while capturing profound emotional resonance.

:

Ek Lamhaa Zindagi

– A Love Story (1938–1979)

:

Biographical romantic drama

: 3.5 stars

:

Juhi Babbar Soni

: Makarand Deshpande and Juhi Babbar Soni

: 90 minutes

Language: Hindi-Urdu (Hindustani)

SHOULD YOU WATCH THIS?

Where to watch: Prithvi Theatre. Sat 26 Sep, 9pm





NameGenreRatingCastDirectorsDurationSolo performances on stage are a demanding theatrical form. An actor has to move between characters, moods, perspectives and emotions, sometimes within seconds, while maintaining complete physical and emotional control.Keeping an audience invested for 90 minutes without a co-performer to share the energy requires a formidable stage presence and an equally strong command of storytelling. Juhi Babbar Soni takes on all these challenges in Ek Lamhaa Zindagi – A Love Story (1938–1979) and gives life to Ekjute Theatre Group’s deeply moving biographical play about her grandparents, writer Razia Sajjad Zaheer and writer-politician Sajjad Zaheer.Directed by Makarand Deshpande and Juhi, the play is rooted in the true story of the couple and has been written by Razia’s daughters Nadira Zaheer Babbar and Noor Zaheer, along with her granddaughter Juhi. The result is a fine amalgamation of emotion, information and wit. More importantly, it brings alive a relationship built on equality, companionship and a shared sense of purpose.And this is not merely a love story, as the title suggests. It journeys through four transformative decades of Indian history, encompassing the freedom movement, Independence, Partition and the post-Independence era.Sajjad's political commitments, imprisonment and prolonged separation from Razia are part of a larger narrative about a couple negotiating love and family against a rapidly changing country.The writing's greatest strength is that it doesn't allow the historical backdrop to completely overshadow Razia's own story. She emerges not simply as the wife of an influential writer and political activist, but as a writer, woman and individual with her own aspirations and emotional landscape.Juhi is at the centre of this experience and handles the transitions with remarkable ease. It is particularly delightful to watch her move from a nine-year-old child to a woman in her late sixties, and then inhabit characters such as her mother-in-law, Lady Boss, and Sajjad himself — entirely through changes in voice, physical expression and emotion, without a single costume change.Yet, the sheer sweep of four decades occasionally makes the play feel information-heavy. A tighter focus on a few emotional moments could've made their impact even more powerful.Still, Ek Lamhaa Zindagi succeeds where it matters most: it turns a family archive into living theatre.Yes, especially if you enjoy intimate, performance-driven theatre that blends personal stories with history and poetry.
Article Summary: Ek Lamhaa Zindagi – A Love Story (1938–1979) is a biographical play about writer Razia Sajjad Zaheer and writer-politician Sajjad Za heer. Starring Juhi Babbar Soni, who masterfully embodies various roles, the narrative intertwines the couple's dynamic relationship with pivotal historical moments.

Article Title: Late night birthday bash on Beed road lands five students in police net
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





A late-night birthday celebration on a public road in Beed ended with five students being briefly detained and their motorcycle seized, after the gathering allegedly disrupted public peace and caused obstruction to traffic.The action by Shivajinagar police on Tuesday night followed a call received by the emergency response number 112 team about a group celebrating a birthday on the road.“A police team rushed to the spot and detained five members of the group. As all five are students, their identities have been withheld. The motorcycle used to place the birthday cake was also seized,” police inspector Sheetalkumar Ballal said.The action was taken under Section 110 of the Maharashtra Police Act. The move comes against the backdrop of increasing late-night birthday celebrations on public roads, where gatherings, loud shouting and bursting of firecrackers or other loud devices have been causing inconvenience to residents.“Such celebrations, particularly around midnight, can disturb residents and affect public peace and order. While celebrating birthdays itself is not an offence, celebrations on public roads that inconvenience others, cause noise pollution or create law-and-order problems will not be tolerated,” Shivajinagar police said, warning that similar incidents would attract strict legal action in the future too.
Article Summary: Five students detained after late-night birthday celebration on a public road in Beed. Police seized their motorcycle and took action under Section 110 of the Maharashtra Police Act. Move comes against backdrop of increasing late- night birthday celebrations on public roads.

Five mild-intensity earthquakes measuring between 2.1 and 2.5 on the Richter scale between 12.30am and 4.30am on Tuesday were recorded in the vicinity of Koyna dam in Patan tehsil of Satara district.The region falls in a seismically active zone, and therefore multiple earthquakes occur in the region. However, most of the earthquakes are not felt, and there is damage caused to the properties. Tremors that are above 3.0 on the Richter scale are normally felt.The first quake was recorded at 12.30am on a scale of 2.1, followed by the second quake- an hour later at a scale of 2.3. The third quake occurred at 3.15am on a scale of 2.5, then at 3.30am, a scale of 2.1 was recorded. The final quake struck at 4.30am at a magnitude of 2.1, with the epicentres located around 48 to 52km from Satara city. These quakes were reported by Satara's earthquake recording station.The earthquake recording station at Koyna dam is currently non-operational, due to which the depth of the epicentre, the longitudes and latitudes could not be ascertained. Earthquake recording and measurement devices are installed at Warna dam as well. Data from three centres: Koyna, Warna and Satara was used to get more details on the quakes.
Article Summary: Five mild-intensity earthquakes measuring between 2.1 and 2.5 on the Richter scale were recorded in the vicinity of Koyna dam in Patan tehsil of Satara district. The region falls in a seismically active zone, and therefore multiple earthquakes occur in the region.

Article Title: LPG leak triggers blast at Sanpada snacks shop in Navi Mumbai, 2 injured
Article Text:
A LPG cylinder leakage caused a blast at a Sanpada snacks shop on Tuesday morning.





NAVI MUMBAI: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in sector-1, Sanpada on Tuesday morning. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.Purushottam Jadhav, Divisional officer of Vashi fire station said, "At 6.13 am, the Vashi fire station received the emergency call informing about a cylinder blast at a snacks shop in Pratik CHS on sector-1, Sanpada. The fire bridge team reached the spot within 5 minutes.It was found that the blast was due to leakage in one of the three LPG cylinders kept at snacks shop. The two men working at the snacks shop sustained severe burn injuries and were rushed to NMMC hospital, Vashi. Those injured were identified as Arjun Yadav (46) who has sustained 75 precent burn injuries and Manish Yadav (26), who has sustained 90 percent burns.The blast even caused damage to two shops adjacent to the snacks shop and three other shops in the neighbouring Abhimanyu CHS. While, the glass facade of Suraj hospital located opposite to Pratik CHS was shattered due to the impact of the blast."
Article Summary: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in Sanpada. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.

Article Title: Khalapur temple theft: Video shows masked man stealing silver Padukas; 2 arrested in Pune
Article Text:
he accused stole silver Charan Paduka from Shree Swami Samarth temple on September 2





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khalapur police probing the theft case wherein a masked man had decamped with a pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city on September 2, have arrested the acccused thief and his aide by tracking them to Pune on Monday.Pradeep Rayannavar, senior inspector of Khalapur informed that, the arrested accused are Mahendrasingh Rathod, 45, who hails from Rajasthan and Ravi Soni, 32, who hails from UP and is a history-sheeter as a theft case is registered against him in Pune.Both were presently residing in Chikhali, Pune district.On September 2, the temple trustee Deepak Bodarde, 68, lodged a complaint of theft of silver Padukas from the temple.When the CCTV footage of the temple premises was checked, it was seen that a masked man wearing a hat and attired in white Kurta-Payjama entering the temple around 7.30am.He goes to the first floor of the temple where the silver Padukas were kept in front of the idol of Shree Swami Samarth.By pretending to offer prayers, he picked up the Padukas and hid them inside his Kurta and exited the temple.Inspector Rayannavar said," The theft was committed when the temple priest had gone to his room near the temple.Upon checking the CCTV footage of the roads near the temple, it was seen that two masked men on a bike were loitering near the temple and conducted a reece before committing the theft.""Considering the religious sentiments of the devotees, Raigad SP forms a special police team to detect the case at the earliest. Subsequently, the CCTV footage along the escape route of the thieves were scanned. The bike used in the crime did not have a registration number plate," Rayannavar added.He further said, "However, using technical expertise, intelligence inputs and footages of CCTV camera along the highways, the thieves on bike were tracked and apprehended from Chikhali in Pune district. We have seized from them the stolen Padukas and the bike used in the crime. On Monday, the acccused were produced before the Khalapur JMFC court that remanded them to police custody till Friday."
Article Summary: A pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city were stolen on September 2. The accused thief and his aide were arrested by tracking them to Pune on Monday.

Article Title: Cop dies by suicide at Navi Mumbai lodge, names ex-DCP, ACP and head clerk in note alleging harassment
Article Text:
The deceased identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening.The deceased, identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli, had recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media.In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.ASI Patil also left behind a nine-page suicide note accusing former DCP (Headquarters) Sanjay Patil, ACP Girish Thakare, and administrative head clerk Jayu Ahire of driving him to take the extreme step by allegedly harassing him while assigning official duties.ACP (Rabale Division) Rahul Dhas said, "ASI Patil had checked into Sachi Lodging and Boarding on Saturday at 4.40 pm. Around 7.30 pm, when the housekeeping staff went to his room, he did not respond, and the door was locked from inside. The lodge manager opened the door with a master key and found ASI Patil hanging from a ceiling fan hook. The lodge manager informed the Rabale MIDC police. ASI Patil was rushed to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead. Prima facie, an accidental death case will be registered at the Rabale MIDC police station."
Article Summary: Pandurang Nimba Patil, a 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police, allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening. He recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media. In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.

Article Title: 12-year-old girl, young woman rescued from prostitution racket in Navi Mumbai
Article Text:
Cops can be seen walking with 2 women. (AI-generated image used for representational purpose)





NAVI MUMBAI: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of Navi Mumbai crime branch rescued a 12-year-old girl and a 26-year-old woman from a prostitution racket being carried out at a lodge in Nerul after conducting a raid by sending a decoy customer on Thursday.The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers by providing them rooms at Kohinoor Palace Lodging and Boarding in Shiravane village, Nerul.Gajanan Kadam, AHTU senior inspector, said the rescued minor girl hails from UP and resided in Shiravane village with her cousins, who had brought her from UP after telling her parents that she would be given a job.The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours after booking a room. The accused demanded Rs 4,000 for supplying a woman.After the accused accepted the amount, the decoy customer signalled the police team waiting outside the lodge, following which they raided the premises.Inspector Kadam said, “The arrested accused are the lodge managers identified as Hridaykumar Singh and Deepak Ramrakhiani and the waiter Kuleshwar Kumar Singh.”At Nerul police station, an FIR was registered against the arrested accused by invoking BNS sections for trafficking of persons and joint criminal liability, along with the POCSO Act, which defines punishment for abetment, such as helping, encouraging or plotting any sexual crime against a child, and the Prevention of Immoral Traffic Act.On Friday, the three accused were produced before the Belapur JMFC court, which remanded them to police custody till Sept 9.
Article Summary: The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers. The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours.
